mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A complete rebuilt Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8 engine typically costs between £8,000 and £12,000 for supply only [EM-QUOTE]. Used units start from around £3,000. Reconditioned units range from £5,500 to £9,000. Prices vary based on the specific engine code (508PN or AJ133) and supplier.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early warning signs of timing chain wear in the 5.0L V8 include a distinct rattling noise from the engine bay during cold starts. Check engine light or camshaft correlation fault codes. Rough idling or slight loss of performance. Metallic debris in the engine oil.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, absolutely. The Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8 is a highly collectible vehicle with current market values ranging from £80,000 to over £130,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. A rebuilt engine cost is a small fraction of the vehicle's total value. It preserves the car's heritage, performance, and resale value. Upgraded rebuilt units address known factory weaknesses.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8 engine supply and fit take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8 engine replacement typically takes 3 to 5 working days. Removal and preparation of the old unit takes 1-2 days. Fitting, calibration, and testing of the new rebuilt engine takes 2-3 days. Nationwide collection and delivery are arranged by the specialist.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the 508PN and AJ133 engines in the Defender 90 Works V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 508PN is the naturally aspirated 5.0L V8 (400-405hp) used in the classic L316 Works V8 editions (2018-2021). The AJ133 is the supercharged 5.0L V8 (525hp) introduced in the newer L663 Defender 90 V8 and Works V8 models (2022-present). Both share similar underlying architecture but have different forced-induction components and tuning.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8 5.0L V8 Requires Attention
problems.affectedModels: Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8 (508PN / AJ133, 2018-present)
problems.rootCause: The rear-mounted timing chain design in the JLR 5.0L V8 family is susceptible to tensioner fatigue and chain stretch over time, which can lead to rattling on cold starts and, if ignored, catastrophic internal damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Endoscope inspection of chain tensioner and guides
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended at 60k miles to catch early wear

repairOptions.longevity: The right call if catastrophic failure has occurred or the block is compromised

At this valuation, a rebuilt engine replacement cost represents a small fraction of the vehicle's total value, making professional replacement highly viable to preserve its collector status.
problems.recommendation: If caught early, a preventative timing chain kit replacement by a JLR specialist is the most cost-effective route. However, if the engine has suffered catastrophic failure due to neglected chain wear, investing in a fully rebuilt unit with upgraded components is the only way to protect the long-term value and reliability of your Works V8.

problems.h4: Coolant Leaks from Crossover Pipes - Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8 Cooling System Vulnerability
problems.affectedModels: Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8 (508PN / AJ133, 2018-present)
problems.rootCause: Plastic coolant crossover pipes and expansion tanks in the V8 valley are prone to becoming brittle and cracking under repeated heat cycles, leading to coolant loss and potential overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of crossover pipes, expansion tank, and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Highly suitable for minor leaks before overheating occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a rebuilt engine with updated cooling components and 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary only if coolant loss has caused severe overheating and warped components

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Given the £80,000-£130,000+ value band of the Land Rover Defender 90 Works V8, minor cooling system repairs are trivial in comparison to the vehicle's worth. However, ignoring a leak can lead to catastrophic failure, making a rebuilt engine the necessary fallback if damage is done.
problems.recommendation: Proactive replacement of the plastic coolant crossover pipes and expansion tank with updated parts is a highly recommended, low-cost preventative measure. If overheating has already warped the cylinder heads, a full rebuilt engine replacement is the safest and most reliable solution.
